clue.text: Rider went, doing a backflip, one that's out of this world

indicators.note: a backflip turns things over, so the rider and the word for went are read backwards together

parts.note: a rider is an addition to a document, like a PS or postscript
went, in the slang sense of relieving oneself, is peed
the ace is the playing card with one pip

explanation.surface: A motorcycle rider showing off with a backflip stunt is hailed as a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went' is the slang sense of urinating, not departing; 'doing a backflip' reverses the rider and that word together.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep space is the region far beyond Earth's atmosphere, literally beyond this planet.

clue.text: One acting to restrain prisoner at first, someone administering drug

indicators.note: restraining someone holds them in, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: someone who acts or does things is a doer

indicators.note: only the opening letter of prisoner is used

explanation.surface: A warder holds back an inmate while someone else injects a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A doper gives drugs, especially to racehorses or athletes, to affect performance.

clue.text: Time to accept motorbike is right for children?

indicators.note: accepting something takes it in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: an eon is a vast stretch of time
Ducati is an Italian make of motorbike

explanation.surface: Asks whether a long stretch on a motorbike suits youngsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling is widely held to be an entitlement every child should have, a basic human right.

clue.text: One with skis shuffling elbows in to nick second

indicators.note: nicking here means getting into, so one piece slips inside the other
shuffling mixes up the letters of elbows in

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second

explanation.surface: Someone on skis shoves past others, elbows out, to grab a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuffling' turns ELBOWS IN into SNOWBILE; 'to nick' puts MO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowmobile is a motor vehicle running on skis at the front and a track behind.

clue.text: Legendary royal butt raised in support of performance by Callas, say?

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits beneath what it holds up

parts.note: Maria Callas was a soprano, so her solo performance is an aria

indicators.note: in a down answer raising a word reads it upwards, backwards

parts.note: a butt is the end of something, like a cigarette

explanation.surface: Suggests a famous rump lifted up to prop up an opera diva's show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns END into DNE, which 'in support of' places below ARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this Cretan princess, daughter of Minos, gave Theseus the thread for the labyrinth.

clue.text: Though sporting wager fails, it's smart

parts.note: though, in the sense of even if, gives even
sporting a hat is being in it, so in

indicators.note: a bet that fails falls apart, so its letters break up and rearrange

explanation.surface: A gambler consoles themselves that a lost sporting bet is a clever one.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal clothes for night-time occasions are smart attire, so the dress itself is what is smart.

clue.text: Articulate call for work in a bakery?

indicators.note: articulating a word speaks it, so the answer sounds like the synonym

parts.note: to call for something is to need it

explanation.surface: Reads like a well-spoken plea for a job at a bakery.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakers work dough with their hands, pressing and folding it, which is exactly what this verb means.

clue.text: Equipment maker extraordinary — sign of quality

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment

indicators.note: read as extra-ordinary, out of the normal order, so the letters of maker rearrange

explanation.surface: Praises an outstanding gear manufacturer as a mark of excellence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges MAKER into EMARK. The Kitemark is the British Standards Institution's certification symbol on approved goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The BSI's kite-shaped symbol certifies that a product meets a British safety or quality standard.

clue.text: One's time is up: with cross to bear, European Community functioning

indicators.note: bearing something is carrying it within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a cross is the letter X
a machine that is functioning is on

explanation.surface: Sounds like a weary bureaucrat's lament that a burden ends the European Community's working days.
explanation.definitionFit: A former convict has completed their sentence; their time inside has been served.

clue.text: Toy club for country park?

parts.note: a dolly is a child's toy doll
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Asks whether a toy golf club would suit a rural park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' is the music: this is the Tennessee theme park owned by country singer Dolly Parton.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolly Parton's amusement park in Tennessee celebrates country music, so it is literally a country park.

clue.text: Set to trap Lancashire opener, old spinner a long way off?

indicators.note: trapping holds something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter of Lancashire

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a veteran spin bowler sets a trap for Lancashire's opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' seems to be a slow bowler from the cricket picture; it is a heavenly body rotating far away.
explanation.definitionFit: This dwarf planet spins on its axis at the outer edge of the solar system, very remote.

clue.text: Same couple hiding imperfection with short name

indicators.note: hiding something keeps it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals, a couple
a dent is a flaw in a surface
Cal is a short form of the name Calvin

explanation.surface: A pair conceals a flaw by going by a nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are alike in every respect are the same, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Trump's extremely furious with free side of Europe

parts.note: an American like Donald Trump might say real for extremely, as in real cool
furious means mad
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: Pictures Donald Trump in a fury about being freed from one part of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' is a sports team: this is the Spanish football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Here side means team; the Madrid club is one of Europe's leading football teams.

clue.text: Black mini's heading off

indicators.note: the heading, or first letter, is taken off

parts.note: dinky means small and neat, miniature, as in Dinky toy cars

explanation.surface: A black Mini car drives away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mini' looks like the car, but it means small: DINKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ink is typically dark, so something coloured like ink is black.

clue.text: American ice hockey player, male perhaps, keeping a lot out?

indicators.note: keeping holds something within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: male is an example of a gender

indicators.note: out means disordered here, so the letters of a lot rearrange

explanation.surface: Describes a hockey player, possibly a man, who keeps plenty of shots out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals the anagram of 'a lot', which splits the gender word after its first letter. Goaltender is the North American word for goalkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: In North American usage the ice hockey goalkeeper is called by this term.

clue.text: Loose packaging is heading for bin, item flatly thrown away?

indicators.note: packaging wraps round contents, so one piece surrounds the others

parts.note: something loose is free

indicators.note: the heading, or first letter, of bin

explanation.surface: Loose wrapping is bound for the bin, a flattened item thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown away' suggests rubbish; it is the toy thrown flat through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: This plastic disc is thrown so it flies flat and level, sailing far off.

clue.text: Halfwit ordered tea, forgetting a coffee

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged
forgetting leaves something out, so a is dropped from tea

explanation.surface: A fool in a café asks for tea and forgets to order a coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' leaves TE from TEA; 'ordered' rearranges HALFWIT with TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso topped with steamed microfoam milk is a popular coffee drink from Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: Try to bury first of remarks that was hurtful, wit long gone

indicators.note: burying puts something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: only the first letter of remarks is used

parts.note: ouch is what someone says when something hurts

explanation.surface: Advice to suppress a hurtful remark, from a comedian long dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho Marx, the comedian famous for quips, died in 1977, so he is a wit of the past.

clue.text: Sign up Republican in party under Ford in the '70s?

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece under another comes after it

parts.note: the Ford Capri was a popular car of the 1970s

indicators.note: one piece sits within another

parts.note: Con is short for the Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Republican signs on to a party led by Gerald Ford in the 1970s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford in the '70s' points to President Gerald Ford, but it is the car.
explanation.definitionFit: The goat is one of the twelve zodiac signs, covering late December to mid-January.

clue.text: Ring in year hugging umpteen lasses, initially

indicators.note: hugging wraps around, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: annus is Latin for year

indicators.note: the first letters of umpteen and lasses

explanation.surface: Someone sees in the new year with plenty of women in their arms.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this is the ring-shaped region between two concentric circles.

clue.text: Stinker with flipping hard heart in journo

indicators.note: flipping turns over, so the word for with reads backwards

parts.note: plus means with, as in a meal plus drinks
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: the middle letters of journo

explanation.surface: A cruel reporter, flipping hard-hearted, is a real stinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reads like a mild curse; it turns PLUS into SULP.
explanation.definitionFit: The element brimstone is notorious for its smell in compounds, like rotten eggs, so it is a stinker.

clue.text: A comedown for transport chief admitting rudeness

indicators.note: admitting lets something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a chief is a head
lip is cheeky talk

explanation.surface: A transport boss is humbled after admitting he was rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comedown' looks like a humiliation; it is a place where a helicopter literally comes down.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing platform for helicopters is where that aircraft descends.

clue.text: Ordinary smell with cylindrical container

parts.note: a hum is British slang for a bad smell
a drum is a cylindrical container, as for oil

explanation.surface: An everyday whiff from a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and routine, lacking variety, synonymous with commonplace.

clue.text: See 5
Mission in Indo-Malaysian uprising

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means read upwards, backwards
the letters sit inside the words Indo-Malaysian

explanation.surface: A rebellion erupting in Indo-Malaysia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters OMALA within Indo-Malaysian; 'uprising' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo in San Antonio, Texas, was a Spanish mission before its famous 1836 siege.

clue.text: Trill around wood in the Land of Nod?

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to trill is to sing
lumber is cut wood

explanation.surface: A songbird warbles near a forest in a dreamland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Land of Nod is a jocular name for sleep, so being there means asleep.

clue.text: Big jar, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: the answer is said the same as the synonym

parts.note: to jar is to grate, as on the nerves

explanation.surface: A large pot that seems to make a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Great is a plain synonym for large or big in size.

clue.text: See 6
Panicky, as windows wound down in the carwash?

definitions.meaning: flustered and agitated, in a state of anxiety

definitions.text: as windows wound down in the carwash?
definitions.meaning: taken literally, someone in a carwash with the windows open would be covered in soapy foam

explanation.surface: A driver's alarm at leaving the windows open during a car wash.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being agitated literally describes being covered in soapsuds, as a horse sweats into foam.

clue.text: Buzzer, physician buzzing?

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, a physician
someone buzzing from the drug ecstasy is on E

explanation.surface: Is the doctor who buzzes the next patient himself a buzzer?
explanation.walkthrough: E is slang for the drug ecstasy, so 'buzzing' gives ON E.
explanation.definitionFit: The male honeybee hums as it flies, so it is a buzzing insect.

clue.text: Knockout award in return for work on computer?

indicators.note: returning reads the combined words backwards

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A boxer's knockout earns a prize, in exchange for some computer work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' looks like a job; it is a literary work read on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A digital book is a written work you read on a computer or tablet.

clue.text: Painter really missing friend, kind to replace one in Monet?

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the friend's letters are dropped from really

parts.note: an ally is a friend

indicators.note: one word takes the place of another inside Monet

parts.note: a brand is a kind or sort, as of soap

explanation.surface: One artist sorely misses a friend, a kindly stand-in for another artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' strips the friend out of 'really', and 'to replace' swaps the three letters spelling 'one' inside the French painter's name for the word for kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt van Rijn was the great Dutch Golden Age painter.
